Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-21 16:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Alice Park (Head of ML, Mistral), Raj Patel (Engineering Manager), Nina Gomez (CISO)

Summary (auto): kickoff POC quality eval scoping. discuss golden prompts, regression sets, hallucination checks, scoring and run cadence.

[00:00] Maya: okay hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. this is Maya from Redwood Inference, i'll hand it off to Liam in a bit to go deeper into the benchmark approach. quick intros?
[00:18] Alice: hi i'm Alice, head of ml at Mistral, we own the customer-facing query pipeline, looking to improve response accuracy and reduce hallucinations for our helpdesk assistant.
[00:27] Raj: Raj here, lead eng, i'll be responsible for data plumbing and running the POC infra.
[00:32] Nina: Nina, security and compliance, i'll be validating KMS and audit log needs.
[00:38] Maya: great. high level objective: 4 week pilot to validate model quality and cost/latency tradeoffs before we decide between hosted or dedicated infra. success criteria we typically see are both quality thresholds and performance SLOs, does that align?
[00:52] Alice: yes, we want to see measurable uplift versus baseline — precision on entity extraction, and a hallucination rate below ~2% on critical intents. latency should stay under 400ms p50 end-to-end but we can be flexible.
[01:11] Liam: quick clarifying Q: when you say hallucination, do you mean factual hallucination on policy/regulatory questions, or extraneous inventing of contact info? that changes the checks we run.
[01:22] Alice: both, but priority is policy/regulatory hallucinations. extraneous info is secondary.
[01:28] Raj: on traffic, we can pull last 30 days, about 120k queries, but we'll need to sample. what size do you need for stable stats?
[01:38] Liam: usually for quality eval we recommend a golden set of 500-1000 canonical cases per intent for scoring, plus a 5k holdout sample to drive regression and load profiling. 5k gives reasonable confidence intervals for aggregate hallucination metrics.
[01:52] Maya: and timing wise we can ingest the samples, run initial model sweeps in week 1, tune configs week 2, larger stress/throughput and final acceptance in week 3-4. propose weekly checkpoints.
[02:06] Alice: sounds good. could you outline what the golden prompts look like? we've had trouble keeping prompt variants consistent across teams.
[02:14] Liam: sure — golden prompts are short canonical prompts plus expected structured outputs. for your use case we'll capture: user message, system persona, few-shot examples when relevant, and expected json schema for the assistant response. we also include negative cases to test hallucination.
[02:31] Raj: about format checks — our downstream parsers are brittle. if the model occasionally drops fields, that's a showstopper. can we enforce schema conformance in the eval?
[02:40] Liam: absolutely — we'll run automated format validation: schema presence, field types, required keys. we'll flag partial-outputs and score them separately. pattern: pass/fail for schema, then quality score for content.
[02:52] Nina: on data security — we need VPC peering or private link for the pilot and KMS for any material we persist. do you support bring-your-own-kms?
[03:02] Maya: yes, for Redwood Private we support customer KMS/HSM integrations and VPC connectivity. for hosted pilots we can provision a private peering and encrypted-at-rest options; persistent logs can be configured to use your KMS in the Private plane. we'll send the security spec.
[03:18] Nina: also SOC2 + audit log retention requirements — we'll share the questionnaire.
[03:22] Maya: perfect. Liam — can you talk through the scoring approach and thresholds?
[03:26] Liam: sure. our typical scoring approach has multiple signals: 1) exact match / schema pass rate (binary), 2) semantic similarity / rubric scores for free text fields (0-5), 3) hallucination binary flags, 4) latency percentiles. we compute weighted composite score per intent with weights customer-specified. For acceptance, we'd propose: schema pass >= 98%, hallucination <= 2% on critical intents, mean rubric >= 4.0, and p50 latency < 400ms. those are starting points.
[04:02] Alice: weights make sense, can we set higher weight on hallucination for regulatory intents?
[04:07] Liam: yes, per-intent weight table. we'll template that and you can edit.
[04:12] Raj: for benchmarks, do you run on open models only by default or do you include quantized variants? cost is a big driver for us.
[04:19] Liam: we run both. initial quality sweep includes a selection of open models and quantized variants where available. for perf/cost we run dedicated-optimized builds and simulate your traffic pattern — burstiness, average seq len. we'll include token-level cost estimates.
[04:36] Alice: curious — how do you simulate prefix caching and KV cache effects? those change latency/cost a lot.
[04:41] Liam: we replay sessions preserving conversation prefixes where possible; our harness supports KV cache warmup scenarios and we can run with/without caching to show delta. we'll note assumptions.
[04:52] Raj: timeline question: if we provide samples by next Tuesday, when would you have a first benchmark?
[04:57] Liam: assuming samples by 2026-10-27, we can produce an initial quality sweep and perf report by 2026-10-29/30; that fits the 4-week cadence with iterative tuning.
[05:08] Nina: what about logging and PII — we need partial redaction. do you offer automated redaction or do we need to preprocess?
[05:15] Maya: you can preprocess or we can help. for pilots customers usually provide anonymized sets; Redwood can also run in a redaction mode but we'd discuss retention windows. we'll include guidance in the security docs.
[05:28] Alice: what does regression testing look like? we want to make sure future model swaps don't regress on golden cases.
[05:34] Liam: regression harness stores golden prompts + expected outputs and runs nightly or on deploy. we compute delta metrics and highlight statistically significant regressions. for the POC we'll run regression on each candidate model and keep a leaderboard.
[05:45] Raj: fine. sample size for statistical significance — is 5k enough to detect a 1% change in hallucination?
[05:51] Liam: 5k gives decent power for several percent changes; detecting 1% at high confidence may need larger sample or stratified sampling of critical intents. We'll propose a small power analysis with your sample distribution.
[06:05] Alice: can you show an example of a golden prompt and the scoring rubric?
[06:09] Liam: yes i'll attach a template after the call. example: Prompt: "User: My refund was charged twice, order 12345, what do i do?" System: persona + schema. Expected fields: intent: "refund_request", entity.order_id: "12345", resolution_steps: list. Scoring: schema pass/fail, entity match exact, resolution adequacy rubric 0-5.
[06:30] Maya: note on deployment choice — if you need predictable SLOs and isolation, Dedicated is recommended; hosted is fastest to start. Both are supported for the POC. any constraints on procurement or timelines?
[06:44] Alice: procurement window is narrow — decision ideally by early December. pilot must demonstrate both quality and cost viability.
[06:52] Raj: also we will need canary style rollout guidance if we switch to production.
[06:57] Liam: we'll include rollout playbook: canary > A/B > full flip with automatic fallback to baseline if regression detected.
[07:07] Nina: last sec — please include retention and deletion controls in the SOW.
[07:12] Maya: noted. recap: Redwood to send golden prompt template, eval rubric, security spec, and initial timeline. Mistral to send sample queries + intent mapping. Weekly syncs and Liam to run the initial bench.
[07:28] Alice: thanks all. we're aligned.
[07:31] Maya: great, will follow up via email.
